t.1.130.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: But Dhṛtarāṣṭra, having heard such words from his son, reflected for what seemed a moment and then spoke to Duryodhana.
t.1.130.2: Pāṇḍu, ever devoted to dharma, was always kind to me and did what was dear to me; so he was toward all his kinsmen, but toward me especially.
t.1.130.4: His son, just as Pāṇḍu was, is likewise devoted to dharma, virtuous, renowned throughout the world, and highly esteemed by the citizens.
t.1.130.3: There is nothing he intends to do, even in matters such as his meals, that I do not know; for he, firm in his vows, constantly makes over the kingdom to me.
t.1.130.6: For the ministers were supported by Pāṇḍu, and the army too was constantly maintained by him; their sons and grandsons as well were supported, and especially so.
t.1.130.5: How could we possibly drag him away from here by force, from the kingdom of his fathers and forefathers, especially when he has allies?
t.1.130.7: Those Paurava people, father, who were formerly honored by Pāṇḍu, why would they not kill us along with our kinsmen for the sake of Yudhiṣṭhira?
t.1.130.8: Thus, father, I pondered this weakness in myself, and seeing it, all the subjects have been won over with wealth and honors.
t.1.130.10: Therefore you should quickly send the Pāṇḍavas away to the city of Vāraṇāvata, by some gentle means alone.
t.1.130.9: Surely they will become my allies, first and foremost; today, O lord of the earth, the treasury together with the ministers rests in my hands.
t.1.130.11: When the kingdom has become firmly established in me, O king, then Kuntī, together with her children, will come back again, O Bhārata.
t.1.130.12: Duryodhana, this same thought turns over in my heart too, but because the intention is sinful, I do not disclose it.
t.1.130.13: Neither Bhīṣma nor Droṇa, nor the Kṣattṛ, nor Gautama will ever consent to the sons of Kuntī being sent into exile.
t.1.130.16: Bhīṣma is always neutral; Droṇa's son stands with me. Where the son is, there Droṇa will be; of this there is no doubt.
t.1.130.14: For we and they are equal in the eyes of the Kauravas, my son; these high-minded men, devoted to dharma, would not wish for anything unjust.
t.1.130.15: How then, father, shall we not come to be fit for slaughter at the hands of these Kauravas and these great-souled ones, and likewise of the whole world?
t.1.130.17: And Kṛpa Śāradvata too will stand wherever these three stand, for he will never abandon Droṇa and his sister's son.
t.1.130.19: So, free of worry, banish the sons of Pāṇḍu together with their mother to Vāraṇāvata this very day; no blame will arise from it.
t.1.130.18: The Kṣattṛ is bound to us by self-interest, but secretly he is on the side of our enemies. Yet he alone is not able to harm us for the sake of the Pāṇḍavas.
t.1.130.20: Terrible, it robs me of sleep, lodged in my heart like a dart; by this deed destroy the fire of grief that has arisen within me.
